subject: Follow-up: Aurora Health — RAG+Agent quickstart templates + observability pack
body:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@aurorahealth.org>
Cc: Maya Rodriguez <maya.rodriguez@aurorahealth.org>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 4:18 PM CST
Subject: Follow-up: Aurora Health — RAG+Agent quickstart templates + observability pack

Jordan/Maya —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week on the “support-agent” workflow (tickets + knowledge base + escalation). As promised, sharing the concrete assets so your team can validate end-to-end quickly.

1) Quickstart templates (RAG, Agents, and combined RAG+Agent)
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts
- Recommended starting point for your use case: the combined RAG+Agent template (retrieval as a tool + planner/executor), since it mirrors your “retrieve policies + draft response + optionally open an internal ticket” flow.

2) Observability pack (dashboards + alert defaults)
- Pack repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-pack
- This includes out-of-the-box panels for p50/p95 latency, token usage/cost attribution, error rates (incl. 429s/timeouts), and trace exemplars so you can click from a request_id into the full trace.

3) What we’d like from Aurora: success criteria + next validation steps
To make the pilot crisp (and avoid “it works, but is it good?”), can you reply with what “success” looks like for the first technical validation?

A few prompts (pick what matters):
- Performance: max acceptable p95 end-to-end latency for chat + RAG (and expected document sizes / top-k)
- Reliability: acceptable error rate, how you want to treat rate limits (429) and timeouts
- Security/PII: what can/can’t be logged (and whether you need stricter redaction defaults)
- Deployment constraints: do you need VPC/Private from day one, or is Hosted OK for initial dev/test with synthetic data?
- Evaluation: what golden questions / test cases should we run to confirm retrieval quality and tool safety

I attached a short checklist we use internally to structure these pilots.

Attachment: AuroraHealth_Redwood_Templates_Validation_Checklist_v0.1.pdf

If helpful, I can also set up a staging org + API key with a slightly higher rate limit for the first week so you don’t spend time fighting 429s while you’re wiring things up.

Best,
Avery

—
Avery Johnson
Account Executive
Redwood Inference



From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@aurorahealth.org>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Rodriguez <maya.rodriguez@aurorahealth.org>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 5:02 PM CST
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Aurora Health — RAG+Agent quickstart templates + observability pack

Avery — thanks, this is helpful.

Initial success criteria (for the first validation pass):

1) Data handling / privacy
- No PHI in prompts during pilot (synthetic only), but we want confidence templates won’t accidentally leak sensitive inputs via logs/traces.
- We need a clear “what gets emitted” list (log fields + trace attrs + metrics) and how to turn down verbosity.

2) Latency + timeouts
- Target p95 < 2.5s for a typical query with RAG (assume 5–10 chunks returned; our docs are long-ish).
- We’ve had issues with streaming getting cut by proxies. If your templates have specific guidance there, that would be great.

3) Retrieval quality
- Not expecting perfect answers, but we want: (a) citations, and (b) no hallucinated policy statements when retrieval is empty.

4) Deployment
- Hosted is fine for the pilot if we can keep it synthetic + in US region.
- Longer term we likely need Private/VPC due to internal audit requirements. Maya will probably ask about audit logs and retention.

Next steps we propose:
- We’ll run the combined template locally + Docker Compose this coming week.
- If that’s successful, we’ll schedule a technical review focused on Private deployment + auditability.

Question: does the observability pack work with standard OpenTelemetry collectors, or is it specific to your Console?

Jordan



From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@aurorahealth.org>
Cc: Maya Rodriguez <maya.rodriguez@aurorahealth.org>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 9:18 AM CST
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Aurora Health — RAG+Agent quickstart templates + observability pack

Jordan — this is exactly the level of detail we were hoping for.

On “what gets emitted” + controlling verbosity:
- The templates are set up for structured logs + traces where request_id/correlation IDs are present, but the guidance is to avoid logging raw prompts/docs by default.
- You can run with minimal logging (errors + high-level counters) while still getting enough telemetry to debug latency/cost.
- We can also align on a “synthetic-only” tagging convention so anything from pilot runs is clearly marked in telemetry.

On streaming behind proxies:
- Looping in Monica (SDK lead) — she can share the recommended timeout/retry defaults and how we handle disconnects (and what to configure when a proxy terminates idle connections).

Observability pack compatibility:
- It’s designed to work with standard OTel (so you can export to your collector), and it also maps cleanly into Redwood Console dashboards.
- If you’re using your own metrics backend today, we can confirm which exporter you prefer (OTLP HTTP vs gRPC).

Pilot plan (suggested) based on your next steps:
1) Run combined RAG+Agent template locally (synthetic) and confirm:
   - citations on every answer
   - “retrieval empty” behavior (no policy hallucinations; responds with a safe fallback)
   - p95 latency vs your target, with top-k=5 and top-k=10
2) Turn on telemetry + import the pack to see:
   - latency split: ingest/retrieve vs model time
   - token usage breakdown for prompt vs completion
   - error classes (including timeouts and any 429s)
3) Private/VPC technical review (60 min): audit logs, retention, region/data residency, and what changes (if any) you’d need from the template to be “Private-ready.”

Two quick questions so we can come prepared:
- What vector DB are you planning to use (or do you want to start with the template default)?
- When you say “long-ish docs,” are we talking tens of pages or hundreds (and what file types)? This impacts chunking + timeouts.

If you can share 6–10 “golden questions” (synthetic OK), we can also run them on our side and compare notes.

Best,
Avery



From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@aurorahealth.org>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Rodriguez <maya.rodriguez@aurorahealth.org>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 10:42 AM CST
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Aurora Health — RAG+Agent quickstart templates + observability pack

Jordan — Monica here (SDK lead). On streaming + proxies, here are the patterns we recommend (and what’s reflected in the templates):

1) Timeouts
- Use explicit connect + read timeouts, and treat “no bytes received for N seconds” as a recoverable condition when streaming.
- For long responses, prefer server-sent events (SSE) / chunked responses with periodic keep-alives so intermediary proxies don’t interpret the connection as idle.

2) Retries/backoff
- For non-streaming requests: safe retry on 429/503 with exponential backoff + jitter.
- For streaming: don’t blindly replay mid-stream (you’ll duplicate tokens). Instead:
  - detect disconnect
  - re-issue the request with an idempotency key (if you have one) and/or with your own application-level “resume” strategy (the templates show the minimal safe approach)

3) Correlation IDs
- The templates propagate request_id/trace context so you can tie client-side disconnects to server-side traces (helps a lot when the proxy is the culprit).

If you can tell us what proxy/load balancer is in the path (NGINX, Envoy, ALB, etc.) and typical idle timeout settings, we can point to the specific knobs that usually fix the disconnect.

Happy to jump on a 30-min working session with your engineers once you’ve run the template once and have initial logs/traces.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
SDK Lead, Redwood Inference
